newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Drilling for samples at Busang goldfield completed.
newsitem.headline: Drilling for samples at Busang goldfield completed.

text.p: Independent drilling at the Busang gold property has been completed, a spokeswoman for the Busang partners said on Monday, bringing closer the answer to whether it is the gold find of the century or a stunning hoax.
The six drillings at Busang were completed on Saturday and the samples will leave for a laboratory in Perth, Australia on Tuesday, spokeswoman Nia Sarinastiti told Reuters.
She said the test drillings were carried out by Canadian mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services.
She was speaking on behalf of the Busang Indonesian Gold JV consortium formed on February 17 to develop the Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province.
Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd has a 45-percent stake in Busang, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States has 15 percent and Indonesian interests the rest.
Bre-X shocked the mining community last month by admitting that there was a possibility the amount of gold at the Busang property had been overstated.
It had earlier put gold reserves at 70.95 million ounces, which would have made it the biggest find of the century.
Bre-X hired the Toronto-based Strathcona to carry out an independent audit to determine the amount of gold at Busang.
Sarinastiti said samples obtained from the drillings were being kept at a locked hangar in the East Kalimantan town of Balikpapan.
She said the results of the sample testing are expected to be known by the first week of May.

"Representatives from all four parties will accompany the samples to Perth," she said, referring to Freeport, Bre-X, the Indonesian government and the Nusamba Group, which has a joint 30-percent stake in the property with a local partner.

The Nusamba Group, headed by Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, is 80-percent owned by three foundations chaired by President Suharto. Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto have 10-percent stakes each.
Industry sources said the testing of the drilling samples would provide the long-awaited answer to the Busang question.
"It could well be the final chapter," one industry official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters. "The testing will show if Busang was the discovery or hoax of the century."
Local newspapers reported on Monday that Indonesia would exclude two applications for contracts of work submitted by Bre-X from a group of contracts to be approved later this month.

Simon Sembiring, head of the sub-directorate of mining development, was quoted by Kompas newspaper as saying Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana planned to approve 68 contracts of work by the end of this month.
He said the Bre-X applications for the southeast and northwest zones of the Busang property had been put on hold.
The contracts are crucial for the further exploration and development of the Busang property.
A ministry official contacted by Reuters declined to comment on Sembiring's remarks, referring questions to the ministry's director-general, Adjat Sudradjat, who could not be reached.

Sembiring also said the government would step up supervision of the mining sector, including limiting the size of concessions and cancelling permits of investors whose programmes were behind or whose calculations were found to be not rational.
